subject: RFP: Dedicated inference reservation — capacity workbook & clarifying Qs
messages:
From: Amy Lin <amy@cloudwave.io>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudWave Procurement <procurement@cloudwave.io>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP: Dedicated Inference Reservation — initial questionnaire

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Please find our RFP questionnaire attached and a short summary below — we are targeting a 12-month reserved commitment for production inference. High-level numbers:

- Primary models: custom Llama-2-70B finetuned for multi-turn chat + a smaller 7B classification model for routing.
- Expected steady-state: 180k tokens/min (avg), ~1.2k qps for short sequences (<=128 tokens).
- Peak/day: 3x steady-state over 4 hour window; expected burst to 6x for event-driven traffic.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms generation time for 128-token sequences.
- Preference: single-tenant reserved GPU pools with kms integration & audit logs.

We attached our completed questionnaire (CloudWave_RFP_Q1_2027.xlsx). Can you provide a preliminary capacity workbook and GPU fitment guidance (A100 vs H100 vs L4), recommended reservation mix, and estimated monthly committed spend? Also include any recommended fallback models for cost control.

We need the deliverable by Dec 10 to feed procurement.

Best,
Amy
Amy Lin
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudWave
amy@cloudwave.io

Attachment: CloudWave_RFP_Q1_2027.xlsx (spreadsheet, 230KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lin <amy@cloudwave.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Inference Reservation — initial questionnaire

Amy — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear targets. We put together a starter capacity workbook and a few clarifying Qs so our sizing is aligned with CloudWave’s traffic profile. Draft workbook attached (redwood_capacity_workbook_v0.1.xlsx).

Clarifying questions:
1) For the 128-token p95 requirement, is that inclusive of network time, or strictly model compute?
2) For the 3x/6x burst windows: are these proportional across all endpoints or concentrated on a subset of routes?
3) Do you expect long-context sessions (>2048 tokens) for a meaningful fraction of requests, or are those rare?

Next steps: Priyom will run throughput simulations against the workbook and propose a GPU mix; Vivek will validate kernel-fitment edge cases. We’ll return a revised workbook + pricing matrix by Dec 7.

—Michael
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_capacity_workbook_v0.1.xlsx (workbook stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Inference Reservation — initial questionnaire

Michael — ran an initial pass on the workbook and attached a short kernel fitment summary. Key observations:

- Model mix: 70B chat (quantized 4-bit) + 7B routing. For p95=220ms at 128 tokens: H100 with TF32/FP8 kernels gives ~18-25% lower latency than A100 for the 70B pass in our microbenchmarks at 512 batch size equivalence. L4 is attractive for the 7B routing model for cost-sensitive routing.
- Baseline sizing (steady-state): recommend 6 H100 cabinets (48 GPUs) to meet 1.2k qps with 20% headroom; this assumes intra-node perf and batching lanes are configured with continuous batching.
- Burst profile: enable a 2x burst pool of mixed L4 nodes for routing + small gen bursts, and allow on-demand spill to regional hosted capacity for the extreme 6x events.
- KV/prefix caching: we'll configure prefix caching for common system prompts — expect ~12-18% token cost savings and improved p95.

I attached kernel_fitment_summary.pdf and updated the workbook cells with throughput assumptions. I also sketched a reservation mix: 65% H100, 25% A100 (fallback), 10% L4 (routing/burst). That balance optimizes p95 while keeping a managed price floor.

Thoughts? Once we have CloudWave’s confirmation on long-context ratio and route concentration, I’ll finalize the GPU counts and the CSV for pricing.

—Priyom
Attachment: kernel_fitment_summary.pdf (report, 420KB)

From: Amy Lin <amy@cloudwave.io>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudWave Procurement <procurement@cloudwave.io>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 07:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Inference Reservation — initial questionnaire

Thanks Michael/Priyom — answers inline to your clarifying Qs: 

- Latency SLO: 220ms p95 should include model compute + queuing; we control edge networking separately so please assume an allowance of ~30ms outside the model runtime.
- Burst distribution: bursts are concentrated on conversational endpoints for marketing pushes — approx 70% of peak traffic targets the chat flow, 30% the routing/aux endpoints.
- Long-context: long-context (>2048) is rare (~2% of requests) but we want correct handling rather than degraded outputs.

I’ve attached our traffic projection CSV (customer_projections_2027q1.csv). The procurement team asked us to prioritize predictability — they prefer a conservative reserved plan with a small buffer for burst.

Can you include in the next workbook: (a) a column that models on-demand spill costs if bursts exceed reserved pool, and (b) a proposed SLA fallback policy (when to spin up hosted fallbacks vs degrade model size)?

Amy
Attachment: customer_projections_2027q1.csv (120KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lin <amy@cloudwave.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Inference Reservation — capacity workbook v1 + pricing

Amy — attached is the revised workbook (redwood_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx) and a reservation_pricing_matrix.csv that models: baseline reserved cost, expected on-demand spill cost, and an example SLA fallback policy. Summary highlights: 

- Recommended reservation: 48 H100 GPUs (6 cabinets) + 8 A100 GPUs as warm fallback + 12 L4 GPUs for routing/burst lanes. This mix hits steady-state p95 targets and gives headroom for 2x burst in-region.
- Expected monthly committed spend (list price estimate, region us-west): $1.15M/mo for the reserved mix; incremental spill estimated at $120k per 2x sustained burst hour across the pool.
- SLA fallback policy (draft):
  * 0-2x burst: scale L4 burst lanes and leverage local prefix cache.
  * 2-4x burst: spin up warm A100 fallback pool (preloaded models) — expected warm-up < 90s for pre-warmed containers.
  * >4x sustained: route non-critical traffic to hosted Redwood API variants (smaller models) and apply cost-based throttling on non-SLA routes.

Attachments include a per-route token-cost breakdown and an example DocuSign term draft link. Let us know if procurement needs a formal SOW.

Best,
Michael
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx (workbook), reservation_pricing_matrix.csv (csv)

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated Inference Reservation — internal next steps

Internal — CloudWave acknowledged the workbook and asked procurement to prioritize predictability. Procurement has a Dec 10 internal decision date, so we should: 

- Send a single-file package (workbook + pricing csv + redlines) to procurement now and include the DocuSign link in the same thread.
- Offer one opt-in demo window for their SREs to validate pre-warmed behavior (Vivek to own).
- Prepare an alternate price band showing a 24-month commit (Laura to draft commercial terms).

I’ll send the package to Amy/procurement in the next 30 minutes. Vivek: can you confirm the pre-warm <90s baseline on H100/A100 by EOD PT? Priyom: finalize the per-GPU perf assumptions in the workbook (cells highlighted).

—Michael
